report.title: Search Demand Report
identity.title: About this report
identity.text: It separates categories and brands and analyses the search volume of related keywords as a time series to show where demand is going. A single keyword's change cannot tell you how a category, brand or product is doing. This skill finds the keyword set that fits the keyword type and diagnoses the demand flow objectively by comparing outside and inside trends.
kpi.title: At a glance
q.external.entity: Compared with competing brands in the same category: did the whole market move together, or only this brand?
q.external.category: Compared with similar categories: did the whole market move together, or only this category?
q.internal.entity: Which product lines within the brand people searched for more or less (the same view as search purposes in category mode)
q.internal.category: What grew or shrank by the purpose people search for together with the target (place, price, form, etc.)
col.name: Name
chart.external.cap: Each line = sum of the bundle's queries (actual monthly search volume) · total = all bundles · click a chip to see only that line with its max, min and latest (click again for all)
hm.title: Monthly change vs the same month last year
hm.cap: Cell = that month's volume ÷ the same month last year − 1 · hatched when last year's value is under 30
share.title: Share by period
verdict.loo.flip: Caution: removing {list} from the comparison changes the conclusion. This is a borderline result that can depend on which {unit} you compare against.
verdict.hold.why: Fewer than 3 outside keywords have a 4-year change, or the seed's 4-year change could not be computed
corr.title: Data notes
corr.dropped: Keywords left out of the tables
corr.rules.text: All values = sum over search engines · compared as 12-month period sums (no projection of the current year; every month appears once per period, so seasonality cancels out) · 4-year change = last 12 months ÷ first 12 months − 1 · first 12 months under 10% of the last 12 months = new · if a keyword first appears within the previous 12-month period, it is marked new instead of a year-on-year change · when Google gives identical values to different keywords they are counted once · the notes below are detection records; values were not changed
top.title: Top {n} queries per bundle
top.cap: Sorted by last-12-month volume · year on year = last 12 months ÷ previous 12 months − 1 · item spelling variants are summed
scope.text.domain: '{src}' is a broad keyword covering many kinds, so candidates were checked with search volume and related queries and the analysis was narrowed to '{seed}' ({how})
scope.text.brand: '{src}' is a brand that sells many items, so candidates were checked with search volume and related queries and the analysis was narrowed to '{seed}' ({how})
purpose.title: Background and purpose
purpose.body: If searches for '{seed}' fell or rose, this report checks whether the whole market moved together or only '{seed}' differs, and what people search for more or less within it. It compares the last 4 years (48 months) of search volume in 1-year periods using ListeningMind {market} search data.
actions.title: Summary
ui.gt.newNoChange: First appeared within the 4 years, so there is no 4-year change
ui.era.prevNewTip: {d} vs the previous period · the previous period is when it first appeared, so it covers only some months
ui.newkw.tip: Number of queries that newly appeared within the 4 years
ui.sb.cap: Bar length = that period's total volume (largest period = 100%) · cells = share within the period · number at the end = period total · top 2 = combined share of the top two in the period · click the legend to toggle items and recalculate · hover a cell for its value
ui.bt.cap: Bar = that period's total ÷ the comparison period's total − 1 · right of the centre line is growth, left is decline · the three 1-year columns share one axis (±100%), the 4-year column uses ±200% · bars beyond the axis are clipped and faded · the {y} values equal the table's year-on-year, the 4-year values equal the table's 4-year column
verdict.tpl.cnt.all.up: all {n} compared {unit} groups grew, with a median 4-year change of {bp}
verdict.tpl.cnt.all.down: all {n} compared {unit} groups declined, with a median 4-year change of {bp}
verdict.tpl.cnt.some.up: {k} of {n} compared {unit} groups grew, with a median 4-year change of {bp}
verdict.tpl.cnt.some.down: {k} of {n} compared {unit} groups declined, with a median 4-year change of {bp}
verdict.tpl.head.same.mixed: {sd} and {pn} moved in a similar way
verdict.tpl.why.same: {mname} {mdir} — {cnt}. {sd} moved similarly at {sp}, so this looks like a market trend rather than something specific to {sd}.
verdict.tpl.me.weak.more: {sd} changed by {sp}, a larger decline than the market
verdict.tpl.why.weak: {mname} {mdir} — {cnt}. {me}, so factors specific to {sd} are more likely than the market.
verdict.tpl.why.strong: {mname} {mdir} — {cnt}. {me}, so {sd} looks stronger than the market trend.
ui.tw.external.cap: Each line = monthly search volume ({engines}) of the queries in that bundle combined (the sum of the queries you see when expanding the table) · All = analysis target and comparison bundles combined · click a chip to see only that bundle with its top 10 queries below — click a query chip for that line only · change is vs the previous year, the last column vs 4 years earlier
ui.ext.cap.lite.entity: Each row is a comparison bundle of brand name × representative item name (both word orders) · every brand on the same basis · click the arrow before a name to expand its queries
ui.ext.cap.lite.category: Each row is a comparison bundle of the category's representative names (up to 2 · incl. spacing variants) · every category on the same basis · click the arrow before a name to expand its queries
ui.ext.cap.full: Each row is a bundle of queries with the same meaning (spelling variants · English · synonyms · same rule as the target) · click the arrow before a name to expand its queries
ui.internal.empty: No inside composition keywords were measured.
ui.pb.title: 1-year change · total and by {unit} (largest first)
ui.if.cap: Each line = monthly search volume ({engines}) of the queries in that {unit} combined (the sum of the queries you see when expanding the table) · All = every {unit} combined · click a chip to see only that bundle with its top 10 queries below — click a query chip for that line only · change is vs the previous year, the last column vs 4 years earlier
ui.it.cap.line: Click the arrow before a name to expand its queries · each query belongs to one product line only (queries naming two lines and queries with exploration or attribute words such as recommendation or women are left out · generation and model names appear as query rows)
ui.it.cap.purpose: Click the arrow before a name to expand its queries · each query belongs to one purpose only (brand → topic → ranking → recommendation → comparison → price → new products)
ui.it.unassigned: · {n} queries that fit no purpose are left out
ui.q.internal.method: Which methods are driving demand within the topic
js.chipTip: Click: show only this line (click again for all)
js.legTip: Click: show only this line (with max, min and latest) · click again for all
js.prevNew: The previous period is when it first appeared, so it covers only some months
ui.modeReason.entity: {share} of {n} related queries contain '{brand}' — most are searches for one brand's products, lines and uses
ui.modeReason.category: In {n} related queries, {k} brands ({top} and others) appear before the item and brand-free modifiers make up {mod} — a generic term spanning several brands
